heading: Foreign Salary in NRE Account Not Taxable for NRIs: ITAT Clarifies
tldr: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Ahmedabad has ruled that foreign salary earned by an NRI outside India is not taxable in India.
This non-taxable status holds even if the foreign salary is credited to an NRE (Non-Resident External) account in India.
The mere deduction of TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) using an Indian TAN (Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number) on foreign income does not make it taxable in India.
The ruling reinforces the principle that an NRI's foreign-sourced income is generally exempt from Indian income tax.
NRIs should ensure their residential status is correctly determined to avoid such tax demands.
caption:
Good news for NRIs! If you earn your salary abroad, it won't be taxed in India, even if you put it in your NRE account. A recent ruling confirms this clear rule. So, if you're an NRI working overseas, your foreign income is generally safe from Indian tax. Make sure your residential status is correct! Read the full article to understand more.
